Lawn Renovation Melbourne: Dethatch, Aerate & Rebuild

Patchy, spongy, compacted or thin? A renovation fixes the problems underneath, so your lawn can grow back thicker and healthier.

Get a QuoteCall 0459 960 501

Written by Dan, qualified horticulturalist and founder of The Mowersaurus

Lawn renovation Melbourne

When a lawn needs more than a mow

Over time, lawns build up thatch (a spongy layer of dead runners), the soil compacts and the grass thins out. Fertiliser and water alone won't fix it. Lawn renovation is how we reset the lawn so it can recover properly.

We offer two levels. A minor renovation resets the mowing height and dethatches the lawn, a great option for lawns that are basically healthy but have grown tall and spongy. A full renovation goes further. We test the soil, apply soil amendments, core aerate, dethatch, scalp and fertilise, rebuilding the lawn from the soil up.

As qualified horticulturalists we time the work around your grass type and the season, so the lawn is growing strongly enough to bounce back fast. For lawn renovation in Melbourne that usually means mid-spring into early summer.

Minor vs full renovation

  • Minor: mowing height reset
  • Minor: dethatching
  • Full: soil testing and soil amendments
  • Full: core aeration
  • Full: dethatching and scalping
  • Full: fertilising to drive recovery

How it works

How a full lawn renovation works

  1. Assess & test

    We look at the lawn and test the soil so we know what we're fixing.

  2. Open it up

    Scalping, dethatching and core aeration remove thatch and relieve compaction.

  3. Feed the soil

    Soil amendments and fertiliser give the lawn what it needs to regrow.

  4. Recover & maintain

    We guide the lawn through recovery, ideally onto a lawn care program.

FAQ

Lawn Renovation FAQs

When is the best time to renovate a lawn in Melbourne?

For warm-season grasses like couch, kikuyu, buffalo and zoysia, mid-spring into early summer is ideal, once the lawn is actively growing. We avoid winter, when the grass is dormant and can't recover.

How long does a lawn take to recover?

A renovated lawn looks rough for the first couple of weeks. With good growing conditions, warm-season lawns typically fill back in over the following weeks. We'll talk you through what to expect for your lawn.

What's the difference between a minor and full renovation?

A minor renovation resets the height and dethatches. A full renovation adds soil testing, soil amendments, core aeration, scalping and fertilising.

Will my lawn need watering afterwards?

Yes. Consistent watering is important while the lawn recovers. We'll give you clear watering instructions for your lawn.
